NKVSW.note: Round 5, kv_slots at matched depth: at reader layers 7/11/19/23/31 the row positions' pre-RoPE K and V are REPLACED by keep x the reader's own + a side-computed slot content read from the side state at the same layer (s(l) = l); zero-initialized slot heads and takeover 0, so update 0 is bit-identical to the input-only K16r1 model (held == deltas_off by construction). Every target token's attention at those layers then reads passage content the side model computed at that depth: the fetch-side test (encoder-decoder cross-attention with the row count as the slot budget), engine mapping = a per-request K/V write into the rows' cache entries. 1/16 warm from K16r1 epoch 2, ND schedule (cosine, warm-up 50), lora-style heads, row-position calibration. The takeovers (keep = 1 - takeover on the reader's own K/V) are the heads' scale parameters and train in the scale group at delta_scale_lr 1e-3 (a scalar under Adam walks ~lr per update: at the encoder rate 1e-4 it could not leave 0.05 within the arm and the arm would replicate NKVWL; at 1e-3 a full replacement is reachable within the epoch). Read: held - deltas_off (must leave 0 and keep separating), intervention_delta_rms per half (the slot content against the reader's own K/V at the rows), intervention_slot_rms (written / own; 1 at init), intervention_takeover (0 at init; rising = the layer discards the reader's own row K/V), intervention_grads. Pairs with NKVWL (additive K/V deltas from the same source: the differences are replacement vs addition and the takeover group) and with NDIAWL / K16r1 (same init, same shared draws).

At reader layers 7/11/19/23/31 every target position from the first row on adds a zero-initialized cross-attention (query = the reader's own residual there, keys/values = the side model's final states at ALL passage tokens; 4 heads of 160 at r = 640) to the layer input; the rows stay as they are. NKVSWn.note: Round 5, kv_slots at matched depth: at reader layers 7/11/19/23/31 the row positions' pre-RoPE K and V are REPLACED by keep x the reader's own + a side-computed slot content read from the side state at the same layer (s(l) = l); zero-initialized slot heads and takeover 0, so update 0 is bit-identical to the input-only K16r1 model (held == deltas_off by construction). Every target token's attention at those layers then reads passage content the side model computed at that depth: the fetch-side test (encoder-decoder cross-attention with the row count as the slot budget), engine mapping = a per-request K/V write into the rows' cache entries. 1/16 warm from K16r1 epoch 2, ND schedule (cosine, warm-up 50), lora-style heads, row-position calibration. The takeovers (keep = 1 - takeover on the reader's own K/V) are the heads' scale parameters and train in the scale group at delta_scale_lr 1e-3 (a scalar under Adam walks ~lr per update: at the encoder rate 1e-4 it could not leave 0.05 within the arm and the arm would replicate NKVWL; at 1e-3 a full replacement is reachable within the epoch). Read: held - deltas_off (must leave 0 and keep separating), intervention_delta_rms per half (the slot content against the reader's own K/V at the rows), intervention_slot_rms (written / own; 1 at init), intervention_takeover (0 at init; rising = the layer discards the reader's own row K/V), intervention_grads. Pairs with NKVWL (additive K/V deltas from the same source: the differences are replacement vs addition and the takeover group) and with NDIAWL / K16r1 (same init, same shared draws). EC2 twin (K16 epoch-2 init; controls A32X 0.322 / WCn 0.122).

NKVSWSn.note: NKVSW plus staged training: the first 200 updates step the slot heads (content and takeovers) only; the encoder, its gates and both LoRAs keep their gradients dropped (no penalty term), then everything trains on the same cosine clock. Read against NKVSW: do the slots open faster when the shared parameters cannot absorb the loss first? Expect grad_norm_reader = 0 and a flat gate trace for 200 updates. EC2 twin (K16 epoch-2 init; controls A32X 0.322 / WCn 0.122).

A32KVSn.note: 1/32 warm from the K16r1 epoch-2 adapters plus kv_slots at matched depth (the NKVSW mechanism): the starved-rows test where the fetch side has the most to gain (A32DnF 0.323 vs the input-only A32X 0.322, deltas off 0.333: every store-side design landed on the control). delta_scale_lr 1e-3 explicitly (A32DL's 0.0 would freeze the takeovers, which train in the scale group); scale_fraction kept but inert. Read held - deltas_off against A32DL (A2 residual deltas, same init) and the control A32W; intervention_slot_rms / intervention_takeover say whether the slots stop being the reader's own K/V. EC2 twin (K16 epoch-2 init; controls A32X 0.322 / WCn 0.122).

NXAWn.note: CEILING MEASUREMENT, NOT A CANDIDATE (not engine-compatible: the reader reads the whole passage's side states, zero compression). At reader layers 7/11/19/23/31 every target position from the first row on adds a zero-initialized cross-attention (query = the reader's own residual there, keys/values = the side model's final states at ALL passage tokens; 4 heads of 160 at r = 640) to the layer input; the rows stay as they are. Bounds what any fetch-side design at these layers can reach: if NXAW does not beat the input-only K16r1 line either, the limitation is not the fetch of the rows. 1/16 warm from K16r1 epoch 2, ND schedule; deltas_off = no delta. Read: held - deltas_off, intervention_attention (out-projection norm per layer, 0 at init), intervention_delta_rms (the delta against the residual at the positions written), intervention_grads (block gradient norms). payload_bytes counts the whole passage. EC2 twin (K16 epoch-2 init; controls A32X 0.322 / WCn 0.122).

NKVTW.note: Round 6, K/V transfer at 4 inner + last (reader layers 7/11/19/23/31): the row positions' pre-RoPE K and V are REPLACED by the SIDE MODEL'S OWN K/V at the same layer and positions, captured after k_norm / v_proj in the side pass (the side runs the rows over the passage with its LoRA, so these carry the passage at that depth in the reader's NATIVE format: side and reader share the base model). K[rows] = (1 - t) x K_reader + t x K_side, t init 1.0 (a full replacement from update 0 - meaningful at init, not an identity; no correction head). Motivation: A32KVSn's learned slot content stayed tiny and the takeover drifted negative (the reader's heads do not read a fresh representation and the reader LoRA cannot re-learn its query side in one epoch); the side's own K/V need no such adaptation. 1/16 warm from K16r1 epoch 2, ND schedule, row-position calibration. Read: held - deltas_off (deltas_off = the reader's own K/V at the rows: the input-only control on the same rows), intervention_takeover per half (1 at init = the side's K/V alone; falling = the layer mixes the reader's own back in; the takeovers train in the scale group at delta_scale_lr 1e-3), intervention_slot_rms (written / the reader's own K/V RMS at the rows; about the side / reader RMS ratio at init), intervention_delta_rms (the transferred content alone against the reader's own), intervention_grads (the takeovers' gradient norm). Pairs with NKVSW (learned slots from the same side states, same init) and NKVWL.

NKVTWA.note: NKVTW at EVERY full-attention reader layer (interventions -1: layers 3/7/.../31, eight layers): the side's K/V of the rows replace the reader's at every layer the reader attends with; the linear-attention layers keep the rows' own states. The engine mapping is unchanged (a per-request K/V write into the rows' cache entries at those layers). Read against NKVTW: does depth coverage matter once the format is native?
